business_problem: CMS needed to cut the cost of storing enormous volumes of log data while still analyzing incidents quickly, retaining historical security evidence, and making the logging environment simple enough for security teams to use effectively.
solution_summary: CMS redesigned its centralized logging platform on AWS to reduce storage costs while improving security analysis and forensic response across massive federal healthcare systems. Log flow data is stored in Amazon S3 buckets, where low-cost object storage preserves historical records, and AWS Lambda sorts incoming data and routes it into the appropriate Amazon OpenSearch Service repositories. Analysts then use OpenSearch dashboards and alerts for near-real-time monitoring, log analytics, and incident investigation. Because the new system keeps historical data available and can queue lost data for reingestion, CMS can replay virtual private cloud flow logs and self-heal more of the pipeline during security issues. The cloud-native design replaced a costlier legacy platform with a simpler-to-use environment that supports daily log ingestion at scale, faster forensics, and stronger access control through OpenSearch and S3 security features.

data_flow: CMS ingests log flow data into Amazon S3, AWS Lambda sorts and routes the data into Amazon OpenSearch Service repositories, and security teams use OpenSearch dashboards and alerts to monitor, investigate, replay, and recover data during incidents.
business_outcome: CMS built and deployed the new logging system in 6 months, cut log-storage costs by 67 percent, ingests 2 TB of log flow data daily, and reduced incident forensics from manual two-week recovery work to an automated replay and self-fix workflow.
